stances.claim: FLP's introduction of the Esmel Fellowships, in partnership with MPIC, deliberately broadens the foundation's reach from its long-emphasized 'liberty' side into the 'prosperity' side of its twin-beacon philosophy -- addressing the entrepreneurial-management-economic-business-law dimensions of 'prosperity under the rule of law.'

Merit-based selection by independent boards of judges (last year, CJ Gesmundo for scholarships; Justice Perlas-Bernabe for dissertations) preserves the integrity of the FLP programs and explains the strong bar-results track record.
stances.rhetorical_move: institutional-credibility framing (the caliber of the judges signals the caliber of the program)

stances.claim: The ultimate FLP projects -- an 'immersive and interactive Museum for Liberty and Prosperity' on the liberty side, and a 'multi-billion-peso Entrepreneurship Fund' on the prosperity side -- are the long-term endpoints to which the current programs build.
stances.rhetorical_move: trajectory-framing (announcing the long horizon to give donors a vision)

stances.claim: Entrepreneurship Fund's goal is 'to help the poor help themselves through private entrepreneurship' -- locating the FLP's anti-poverty model in private-sector self-help rather than direct subsidy.
stances.rhetorical_move: self-help anti-poverty framing (private-sector route to prosperity)

notable_anecdotes: Acronym genesis of 'Esmel': Entrepreneurship, Sustainability, Management, Economics, business Law -- explicitly built so that the five new MPIC-partnered fellowships map onto each letter of the prosperity-philosophy framework.
Per-grantee Esmel package: P350,000 tuition + P100,000 books/stipend = P450,000, deliberately structured to allow stacking on top of fellowships from other entities (merit-based, not need-based).

Eligibility restriction in the legal scholarship: only open to law schools that scored above the overall bar passing rate in the most recent bar -- using the Office of the Bar Confidant's statistical data as the cutoff.

Dissertation Writing Contest prize structure last year: P320K first (Cuntapay, ADMU), P220K second (Baliong, USC), three third-placers at P120K each (De Vera/DLSU, Dulanas/USC, Lim/ADMU) -- published in full at libpros.com.

Disclosure of FLP board composition: former DepEd secretary Edilberto de Jesus, retired SC Justice Angelina Sandoval-Gutierrez, former BSP Governor Amando Tetangco Jr., lawyer Joel Emerson Gregorio, Prof. Elenita C. Panganiban, Maria Elena P.S. Yaptangco, and lawyer Sean James Borja -- with CJ explicitly as chair.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban announces a deliberate expansion of the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity into the 'prosperity' side of its twin-beacon philosophy through the new Esmel Fellowships -- Esmel being an acronym for Entrepreneurship, Sustainability, Management, Economics, and business Law -- funded with Metro Pacific Investments Corporation via the Metro Pacific Investments Foundation, awarding P450,000 per grantee (P350K tuition + P100K books/stipend) to five qualified applicants enrolled in MBA or MS-equivalent programs at AIM, ADMU, DLSU, UP, or UST. He restates the continuing programs -- the sixth-year Legal Scholarship Program (with Tan Yan Kee Foundation, P200,000 per scholar across at least 20 law students from schools above the overall bar-passing rate) and the Dissertation Writing Contest (with Ayala Corporation, open to upper-year law students and LLM candidates) -- and credits last year's independent boards of judges chaired respectively by Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo and Senior Justice Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe. He documents the prior year's cohort in full -- 21 scholars across FEU, St. Louis, UP, UCor, U of Cebu, UST, USC, DLSU-Manila, FSUU, and ADMU; and dissertation winners led by Lord Jay-em Cuntapay (ADMU, P320K first prize) and Eunice Baliong (USC, P220K second). He discloses the FLP Board of Trustees (de Jesus, Sandoval-Gutierrez, Tetangco Jr., Gregorio, Panganiban, Yaptangco, Borja, with CJ as chair) and reiterates the foundation's 2011 founding mission to 'safeguard liberty and nurture prosperity under the rule of law,' closing with the foundation's two long-horizon endpoints: an 'immersive and interactive Museum for Liberty and Prosperity' on the liberty side, and a 'multi-billion-peso Entrepreneurship Fund' on the prosperity side -- the latter framed as 'a program to help the poor help themselves through private entrepreneurship.'
